title: Component stickerbook and interaction safety spec
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Create a compact, developer-consumable component stickerbook (Figma library plus token mapping) with an ‘interaction safety’ spec that documents required states, keyboard behaviors, motion fallbacks, and failure-mode affordances across cost/dashboard panels and rollout controls.

Context: We have many one-off components across cost views, rollout rails, and metric tiles. Engineering teams need a single source of truth for variants, props, and accessibility constraints so runtime implementations (hosted + dedicated + private) can maintain consistent behavior and pass audit. This ticket collects decisions, produces the Figma library, and defines the acceptance criteria for handoff.

Deliverables: 1) Figma stickerbook with 120+ components (cards, chips, pill states, compact toggles, micro-rail controls, status badges) and 5 density variants; 2) Interaction Safety Spec (MD/Confluence) covering keyboard nav, focus ring, aria patterns, error/responsive layouts, and graceful degradation for reduced-motion and high-contrast; 3) Token export mapping (color, spacing, elevation, motion tokens) with examples and migration notes; 4) Dev handoff bundle (tokens.json, CSS vars, component prop table) and a small acceptance checklist for QA.

Trade-offs/Decisions: - Chose a single base Card component with composition props instead of multiple card variants to reduce implementation surface; trade-off is slightly more prop logic in runtime wrappers. - Selected semantic tokens for intent (success/warn/error/info) rather than per-component hardcoded colors to simplify theming for Private deployments. - For compact density, prioritized readability at small sizes over additional metadata; cost inspector panels will show abbreviated labels at <240px.

Acceptance criteria: - Figma library published to the org team with version bump and public link. - Interaction Safety Spec reviewed and signed off by Accessibility lead (AA) and Platform PM. - Tokens exported in the agreed JSON schema and referenced in one sample component PR. - 5 internal engineers can implement components from the prop table without additional design clarification (usability trial).

Notes on implementation coordination: Align with ENG routing for rollout-rail props (ENG-8871) and confirm Console release window console-2025.04 for publishing. Include a short migration guide for teams using legacy cost cards (DES-4371 reference).
